subject: Pilot candidate slate, ops playbook, and risk controls
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@aurelia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot candidate slate, ops playbook, and risk controls

Samir / Aurelia team — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a recommended path so we can get a pilot moving next week. Keeping this tight so your execs can skim and we can lock dates.

Summary of recommended slate (shortlist):
- Model A (quantized): strong on throughput, best cost/unit (approx $0.6 per 1k tokens in our Dedicated profile), median p95 latency ~120ms for 512-token sequences. Good for bulk summarization and classification tasks.
- Model B (higher-capacity): best quality on long-form generation (ROUGE + human eval delta +5 points vs Model A), higher token cost (~$1.8 per 1k) and p95 latency ~300ms; recommended for user-facing composer flows.
- Model C (fallback distilled): extremely low-cost and low-latency (p95 ~80ms), weaker on edge-case hallucination metrics but good for quick retrieval-augmented replies. Good as a safety/first-pass tier.

Why this slate?
- Balance: Model A gives predictable throughput for batch/async jobs; Model B preserves quality where user experience depends on nuance; Model C keeps unit-cost low and provides a graceful degrade.
- Ops: all three have quantized variants that we can deploy to Dedicated or your VPC. We recommend enabling automatic routing policies that prefer Model B for personas flagged as "high-value" and fallback to C on timeouts.

Key artifacts attached: redwood_benchmarks_may27.pdf (per-model latency/cost/qual tables), prompt_set_e2e_v2.jsonl (recommended prompt templates for each intent), pilot-m-a-matrix.xlsx (mapping of milestones to owners).

Risks and regression controls we propose:
- Quality drift monitoring: run the provided eval set (in Drive link) daily during pilot; alert on >3% drop in correctness on the safety prompt slice.
- Canary traffic split: 5% -> 25% -> 100% rollout for Model B to measure real traffic latency tail and token spend.
- Fallback policy: 300ms hard timeout to return response from Model C to preserve SLA.

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm pilot scope (3 intents: summarization, reply-synthesis, and suggestions) — reply with any scope edits.
2) Confirm budget envelope for first 30 days (suggesting $12k committed to Dedicated + pay-as-you-go overflow).
3) Identify Aurelia eng ops owner to accept VPC peering and KMS details — cc ops@aurelia.ai if ready.
4) We’ll provision a pilot workspace and send a DocuSign SOW link by Monday.

If agreeable I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Eng/Prod on Tuesday.

— Rafael

- For budget: $12k is in line but we need a conservative cap; suggest a $18k hard cap to include overflow.

Samir — great questions, answered inline: 

1) Factuality checks in the prompt set: we marked 12 prompts as "factuality probes" in prompt_set_e2e_v2.jsonl (prefix: FACT_PROBE). Those are the ones we run against ground truth and human labels nightly. They’re in the Drive folder under /evals/factuality.

2) Budget cap: $18k hard cap is fine. We’ll set billing alerts at 50% and 80% thresholds and the account will be paused at hard cap unless you authorize overflow.

3) Hallucination alerting: recommended configuration —
- Metric: %incorrect_facts on FACT_PROBE slice (rolling 24h)
- Thresholds: 2% (warning) / 4% (critical) relative to baseline from day 0
- Channels: PagerDuty for critical, Slack channel #aurelia-llm-alerts for warnings and triage items
- On critical: automatic rollback to Model C for affected intents and open an incident in our Ops console with traces and sample queries.

We’ll include these as default monitors in the pilot workspace.

If that works I’ll send the DocuSign SOW and a calendar invite for the Tue kickoff (30-min).

— Rafael

Quoted message included for thread continuity.

Subject: Re: Pilot candidate slate, ops playbook, and risk controls — technical notes

Quick technical note from infra/SE side to surface before we kick: 

- Quantized Model A: in our Dedicated profile we recommend the 8-bit kernel build (Q8) for 512-length sequences. It keeps p95 tails stable at scale — we tested at 12k concurrent tokens/sec.
- Model B: for long-form, ensure KV cache capacity is 24GB per replicate; otherwise p95 tail moves from ~300ms -> ~520ms under burst. That’s the primary ops ask (we’ve surfaced a pre-sized machine type in the pilot workbook).
- Prompt stability: the prompt_set_e2e_v2 contains templated guardrails (prefix instructions + <FACT_CHECK> block). SE recommends versioning prompts in the pilot workspace to allow rollback per-change.

Operational checklist for kickoff (we put owners in pilot-m-a-matrix):
- Peering and KMS key exchange (Samir / Eng Ops)
- Pilot workspace access and eval harness (Ben / Marissa)
- Canary routing rules + SLO config (Tessa / Aurelia Prod)
- Billing cap and alerting (Rafael + Aurelia finance)

I’ll attach a short ops runbook to the Drive folder and we’ll pin the important knobs.

— Ben
